The collision diagonal is the full induced simplicial subcomplex of vertices p_uu and c_ee; dividing barycentric mass by the total off-diagonal weight yields a continuous equivariant strong deformation retraction of the deleted product onto the full off-diagonal subcomplex K, remaining collision-free throughout. Barycentric subdivision makes group action without inversions. Each face chain uses at most two original vertices per bipartition side, and every such equality pattern extends to a full side permutation, so orbit-chain combinatorics depends only on equality of m,n for m,n>=2. I independently rebuilt the product triangulations and complete group actions for representative (2,2) and (2,3) and validation cases (3,3),(3,4), finding 4/5/2 and 6/9/4 face orbits, respectively; chain-orbit quotient simplices have f-vectors (11,22,12) and (19,42,24) with no duplicate keys, links intervals/circles, one 8-edge or 12-edge boundary circle, χ=1, hence PL disks. I also read the original quotient_models.json certificate and separately replayed every one of its 22 and 42 free-face collapse pairs; each elementary collapse has exactly one current coface and ends in a vertex. This establishes the compact disk retract and contractibility of the noncompact original full symmetry quotient; NO homeomorphism to a compact disk is claimed.
